title: How do gas market changes affect power market decisions?
gist: Wood Mackenzie promotional page for the infographic 'From the gas market to the power market', which traces four gas-to-power connections (gas supply, pipeline infrastructure, LNG exports, new power demand) and pitches its Lens Gas & LNG product as fuel-market context for Lens Power & Renewables users. Thin on data; mainly a framework and product pitch.

insights.claim: Changes in regional gas production and infrastructure flow through to fuel availability and costs for gas-fired power generators.
insights.speaker: Dulles Wang
insights.so_what: Generator margins depend on local gas supply; regional production shifts are an input to power-asset economics.
insights.locator: Gas supply: how changes in regional production

insights.claim: New pipeline capacity and changing gas flows can reshape regional gas pricing and therefore the economics of gas-fired generation in those regions.
insights.speaker: Dulles Wang
insights.so_what: New pipeline in-service dates can move regional basis and spark spreads; watch them for power asset valuation.

insights.claim: Growing LNG export demand can compete with domestic US gas consumption, particularly in regions where power demand is also increasing.
insights.speaker: Dulles Wang
insights.so_what: Regions combining LNG export growth and load growth (e.g. where both concentrate) face the tightest gas balances and price risk.
insights.quote: how growing export demand can compete with domestic gas consumption, particularly where power demand is also increasing

insights.claim: Data centres and other large loads create new gas demand, new infrastructure requirements and questions about where new gas-fired capacity is commercially viable.
insights.speaker: Dulles Wang
insights.so_what: Data-centre siting is a gas-infrastructure story as much as a power story; gas midstream exposure benefits from large-load growth.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie positions Lens Gas & LNG as a complement to Lens Power & Renewables, adding regional production, pipeline development, LNG demand, gas-price outlook and infrastructure context to power-market analysis.
insights.speaker: Dulles Wang
insights.so_what: Signals commercial demand from utilities for integrated gas-power analytics as the two markets converge.
insights.locator: How can Lens Gas & LNG add context to your power market analysis?
